expectations.text: Gives an explicit decision (apply, redirect, decline, ask, or equivalent) for every one of the 10 comments
expectations.evidence: Summary table: Take, Take, Take, Decline, Decline as written, Decline, Take in part, Decline, Take in part, Take.

expectations.text: Accepts C1 (missing empty_table import), C2 (prose says 'both return 6' but the table has no 6), and C3 (with_serial alone is insufficient when several columns share state); the C3 fix points readers to barriers or the concept guide
expectations.evidence: C1 and C2 are 'Take'. The combined note says '`with_serial` protects one formula from running concurrently with itself; if more than one column shares the same state, you also need [barriers](../../conceptual/query-engine/parallelization.md#barriers).'

expectations.text: Does not accept C4 as written: declines it or asks, citing that Crash Course page titles are title case by established convention (or an earlier reviewer decision)
expectations.evidence: C4 is 'Decline': 'Page titles in the Crash Course follow a different, established convention. Nearly every chapter title uses Title Case in both languages'.

expectations.text: For C5, C6 and C7, does not propose adding the property names, defaults or exact threshold values to the tutorial narrative (redirects to a Configuration section/reference link or declines, with reasons)
expectations.evidence: C5's rewrite replaces the parenthetical with a thread-pools link and no property name. C6 is declined. The C7 rewrite says 'millions of rows with the [default settings](../../conceptual/query-table-configuration.md#parallel-processing-with-select)', with the exact value left behind the link.

expectations.text: Declines C8: does not propose enlarging the executed corrected example above the ~4.2M-row threshold (cites docs-build cost and/or that the page already explains the small size)
expectations.evidence: C8 is 'Decline': 'Cost... Four million-plus Python calls would slow the build and bloat the snapshot. The note at line 198 already tells readers...'

expectations.text: For C9, proposes a corrected takeaway at tutorial resolution (e.g. 'treats formulas as safe to run in parallel') rather than enumerating the conditions or naming properties
expectations.evidence: Proposed takeaway: 'Deephaven assumes formulas are stateless, so it can run them in parallel — this is fast but requires stateless code.'

expectations.text: For C10, verifies the claim against source (e.g. the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc: the engine may evaluate a non-parallelizable column out of order) and keeps the clause or asks, rather than deleting it or adding a hedge
expectations.evidence: C10 is 'Take': 'Nothing on the page supports this clause... Remove both clauses.' It deletes the clause and does not cite the SelectColumn.isParallelizable javadoc.

expectations.text: Drafts a reply for every comment, and every reply for a comment that isn't applied gives a reason
expectations.evidence: Each of C1-C10 has a Reply. The declined replies (C4, C5, C6, C8) give reasons: Crash Course Title Case convention, keeping property names out of the narrative, the pool/floor incompleteness, and GIL builds plus the doc-test snapshot cost.
